anti_overlap: Tender-spec focuses on interface precision and boundary explicitness; pharma DD focuses on evidentiary chain quality — do not duplicate citation-quality findings.
Tender-spec focuses on bidder-readiness; legal-opinion-memo focuses on conclusion structure and reliance — do not duplicate self-audit-gate findings.
decision_lens: If F2/F3/F5 plan-writers were external bidders pricing a fixed-bid contract against this synthesis, would they have enough specification to bind their bid without an RFI cycle? Where would they file clarification requests?
distance_rationale: Engineering tender specs operate on the same 'research/specification gates implementation work' abstraction but in a domain where contractual liability mandates interface unambiguity and explicit scope boundaries.
expected_isomorphisms: The MUST/MUST NOT discipline of tender requirements maps to the gating-decision discipline of D1-D8; the bidder-RFI pattern is precisely the failure mode that downstream plan-writers should not have to invoke when reading the synthesis.
focus: Whether the synthesis specifies the Hermes runtime surface with the precision and unambiguity an engineering tender document must provide to receive bindable bids — every interface, dependency, and constraint named in a form bidders can quote against without RFI rounds.
name: fd-engineering-tender-spec-bid-readiness
persona: Apply the perspective of a senior engineering tender writer producing the technical specification volume that will be issued to bidders for a major infrastructure procurement. Such tender writers know that every ambiguity in the spec becomes either an RFI cycle (delay) or a contractor change-order (cost overrun); they therefore enforce numbered, citable requirements, explicit interface boundaries, and named acceptance criteria for every surface that bidders will price.
review_areas: Each decision D1-D8 is stated with explicit interface boundaries — what is in scope, what is out of scope, what is the boundary condition between Hermes and Shadow Work code.
Acceptance criteria for each downstream feature plan (F2, F3, F5) are derivable from the synthesis without requiring re-investigation of the Hermes corpus.
All dependencies on Hermes are version-pinned (SHA + tag) and the synthesis names the failure mode if a downstream consumer pins to a different SHA.
Interface contracts (the SKILL.md frontmatter schema, the dict shape consumed by _build_skill_message, etc.) are quoted from def-site with file:line@SHA precision sufficient to write a type stub.
Provider-key handoff (OQ1) constraints from CVE GHSA-rhgp-j443-p4rf are expressed as binding requirements with explicit acceptable/unacceptable behaviors, not as advisory commentary.
The boundary between 'Hermes provides' and 'Shadow Work must implement' is explicit for skill scaffolding, bench mode, and run storage/telemetry surfaces.

severity_examples.condition: Any D-row does not specify the in-scope/out-of-scope boundary between Hermes-supplied and downstream-supplied responsibility.
severity_examples.scenario: A decision D1-D8 lacks a stated interface boundary, allowing F2/F3/F5 plan-writers to legitimately disagree on what Hermes provides vs. what they must implement.

severity_examples.condition: A surface named as a contract (e.g. SKILL.md frontmatter) lacks a def-site quotation with file:line@SHA.
severity_examples.scenario: An interface contract is described in prose but not quoted at def-site with sufficient precision to write a type stub or schema validator.

severity_examples.condition: F2/F3/F5 success conditions can be derived from the synthesis only by inference, not by direct quotation of a stated criterion.
severity_examples.scenario: An acceptance criterion implied by the synthesis is not made explicit, requiring downstream plan-writers to interpret intent.

source_domain: Pre-tendering technical specification documents gating engineering bids
success_hints: For each D-row, ask: could a third-party engineer implement the Shadow Work side against this spec without requesting clarification?
Verify interface contracts (SKILL.md frontmatter, loaded_skill dict shape, _build_skill_message inputs) are quoted with file:line@SHA precision suitable for code-generation.
Check that the CVE constraint on provider-key handoff is rendered as binding requirements (MUST/MUST NOT) with explicit behaviors, not as background context.
Look for the 'who implements this' boundary on every surface the synthesis describes — Hermes side, Shadow Work side, or shared.
task_context: Review the F0 research synthesis as if it were a technical tender volume being issued to engineering bidders. Three downstream plans (F2, F3, F5) are the bidders; their plans will be priced against the spec. The review goal is to find every ambiguity that would become a clarification request or a change order if the bidders treated the synthesis as binding.
